name: Word-by-word editing on a scrub timeline
looks: A headline stacks in naming what the product does to every word. It cuts to an editor view: a filmstrip of small frame thumbnails sits above a word-chip row and a waveform, a playhead marker sitting on one selected word-chip, highlighted, among the others.
build: list-stack-reveal for the headline. The editor reuses timeline-scrubber-hud's playhead-on-track mechanic, but the track is a row of individual word chips rather than scene markers; the selected chip gets a filled background and the waveform beneath pulses in sync with the audio level under the clock.
sound: A tick per headline line, then a soft scrub tick as the playhead's selected chip changes.
prompt: Prove word-level control: show an editor where every spoken word is its own selectable chip above a waveform and a filmstrip, one chip highlighted as the playhead sits on it, to say the product understands speech at the level of individual words, not just lines.
